Every original risk is repeated here with its disposition after independent re-verification. New risks found during this review are appended at the end (R-019 onward).

risks.evidence: Independently reconfirmed: fix present in preflight.py (_stage_writable_checkpoint_for_smoke_test), regression test present and passing. Base checkpoint hash reverified as unchanged after this review's own additional real Docker/GPU activity (two more preflight runs, one optimizer-continuity probe).

risks.evidence: Independently reconfirmed: is_resume parameter and STATUS_COMPLETED/STATUS_FAILED rejection present in launch_guard.py, tests passing.

risks.title: Launch guard never checked whether the code commit had changed since prepare
risks.evidence: Independently reconfirmed: current_code_revision/allow_code_revision_drift present and tested. Demonstrated live a second time in this review: the run prepared for the original audit (commit d33a32e) is now itself stale relative to this review's own commit (bf9a53a); the guard correctly refuses it without an override, exactly as designed.
risks.required_action: Do not launch the stale run (training/full-corpus-20260801T192341Z); use the fresh one prepared in this review (training/full-corpus-20260801T213023Z).

risks.title: TrainingSessionState.global_step is never incremented and is always 0
risks.opus_classification: CORRECTED -- confirmed true, but the underlying reality is worse-but-not-dangerous: the REAL optimizer.iterations value (not just ArchiveTrust's own bookkeeping field) is ALSO always 0 at the start of every real container invocation, empirically confirmed in this review by loading two real pilot checkpoints and inspecting the restored optimizer directly. global_step=0 is therefore not a bookkeeping gap hiding real growth -- it is (accidentally) consistent with what actually happens. See R-019 for the full, corrected finding.
risks.evidence: Independently reconfirmed via fresh grep (no assignment site exists). Superseded by the direct empirical test described in R-019.
risks.required_action: Relabel/document rather than silently leave as an unexplained 0 -- see R-019's required action, which subsumes this.
risks.accepted_risk: The field's absence of real tracking does not gate resumability in practice, since resumability depends on the checkpoint file (weights), not this field -- see R-019.

risks.title: The pilot's resume-proof 'global_step_continued_not_restarted' field actually re-tests epoch continuity
risks.opus_classification: CORRECTED AND DEEPENED -- confirmed true (the naming bug is real), but this review found the underlying claim the field's NAME makes (global-step/optimizer continuity) is not merely unverified, it is FALSE, empirically. See R-019.
risks.evidence: Independently reconfirmed verbatim at training_session.py:575. Superseded by the direct empirical test in R-019, which shows the real optimizer state does not continue at all -- not just that this particular check fails to prove it does.
risks.accepted_risk: See R-019 -- the pilot's own real, successful 22-epoch result is direct empirical proof the actual mechanism (weights persist, optimizer state resets) works for this model/task, independent of what this specific proof field claims.

risks.title: random_seed can silently diverge between persisted state and what is used on resume
risks.evidence: training_session.py::run_training_session now raises ValueError on a random_seed mismatch on resume, exactly mirroring the existing configuration_hash check. Two new tests pass (test_refuses_to_resume_under_a_changed_random_seed, test_resuming_with_the_same_random_seed_succeeds); full test_training_session.py suite (25 tests) passes.

risks.title: Launch guard's shard-integrity check is self-referential; only validation overlap re-checked at launch, never test overlap
risks.evidence: launch_guard.py::recompute_real_shard_hash() now reads every real lap-0 shard file's actual line_id column and independently reproduces the hash, rather than re-reading the same cached summary field. A symmetric test_manifest_path overlap re-check was added. Proven with a real tamper test: a real lap-0 shard file was overwritten with foreign content while leaving sharding_summary.json untouched, and the new check correctly detected the drift and the guard correctly rejected it. Verified with zero false positives against the real, current, untampered 171-shard set (a live dry-run).

risks.title: verify_checkpoint performs only structural zip validation, never a functional load, for real production checkpoints
risks.opus_classification: PARTIALLY RESOLVED -- the underlying question ('can a real production checkpoint be functionally loaded') is now answered YES with direct evidence, via this review's own optimizer-continuity probe, which performed a genuine tf.keras.models.load_model() round trip against two real pilot checkpoints on the real GPU. The narrower implementation gap (verify_checkpoint() itself still only does the cheap structural check during a real run) remains, by design, for performance reasons.
risks.evidence: This review's Phase 2B/2E probe: both real checkpoints loaded successfully with the exact custom_objects dict main.py itself uses (found by reading main.py:72-75 directly).
risks.required_action: None required for launch. Optional hardening: an operator-triggered functional verification could be added as an explicit, occasional check (e.g. once per lap) rather than every shard, if desired.
risks.accepted_risk: A checkpoint that passes the cheap structural check but fails to functionally load is still caught, one shard later, by the existing epoch_failed safe-stop path -- not silently.

risks.opus_classification: SUPERSEDED BY R-019 -- the source-code analysis this finding relied on reached an INCORRECT conclusion (that the mechanism was sound). Direct empirical testing in this review shows the opposite: no cross-shard LR decay or optimizer continuity occurs. See R-019 for the corrected, evidence-based finding and its non-blocking resolution.
risks.evidence: Superseded -- see R-019.

risks.title: No checkpoint retention policy and no mid-run disk-space monitoring; prepared plan needs more disk than was free at the time of the original audit
risks.opus_classification: CAPACITY COMPONENT RESOLVED; OPERATIONAL HARDENING COMPONENT REMAINS, NOW ACCEPTED RISK
risks.evidence: Independently measured: free space is now 322,731,458,560 bytes (300.57GiB/322.73GB), up from ~95.4GB at the time of the original audit -- the operator's claim of freeing ~300GB is verified, not assumed. Per-shard cost independently re-derived from individual epoch directories (not just an average): exactly 711MiB/epoch across 6 sampled epochs (1,5,10,15,20,22), confirming (not revising) the original estimate. Recalculated requirement for the full 171-shard plan: 127.44GB (previously 124.4GB, using the more precise per-shard figure). Remaining reserve after the full plan: 194.92GB, a 61% margin. Docker's own storage (72.7GB) independently confirmed to live on the C: drive, not D:, so it does not compete with this budget.
risks.required_action: None blocking. Recommended, not required: implement a checkpoint retention policy and mid-run disk monitoring before relying on this workflow for future, larger, or longer-running retraining cycles, since the current large margin is a consequence of the operator's manual disk cleanup, not a structural guarantee.
risks.accepted_risk: No retention policy, no mid-run monitoring, no live-tested disk-full recovery path -- all real, but no longer blocking given the ~195GB reserve and the code-level confirmation (this review's own analysis) that the atomic-write pattern used throughout the codebase prevents corruption even in an untested disk-full scenario (it crashes loudly rather than corrupting data).

risks.title: Optimizer momentum and the learning-rate schedule do not survive any shard/container boundary -- empirically confirmed, not merely unverified
risks.impact: Every real container invocation (main.py:103-119, .loghi-upstream/loghi-htr/src/main.py) unconditionally constructs a brand-new lr_schedule and optimizer and model.compile()s it onto the loaded model, discarding any optimizer state tf.keras.models.load_model() may have restored. Confirmed empirically: two real checkpoints from the completed pilot run, four real epochs apart, both show optimizer.iterations=0 and lr=0.0001 unchanged. Model WEIGHTS do continue correctly (real, monotonic 22-epoch CER improvement in the pilot; also directly observed as real, non-trivial tensors in this review's own probe). The recorded learning_rate_policy='constant_0.0001_decay_0.99' label is factually inaccurate for the multi-shard run -- there is no continuous cross-shard decay, only a small, resetting, in-shard sawtooth.
risks.evidence: Real probe against training/loghi-swedish-v1/run-state/epoch_output/epoch_1/model_new10/best_val/model.keras and .../epoch_5/model_new10/best_val/model.keras, loaded via tf.keras.models.load_model() with the exact custom_objects dict main.py itself uses (CERMetric, WERMetric, CTCLoss, ResidualBlock, LoghiLearningRateSchedule -- found at main.py:72-75). Both real checkpoints: optimizer=Adam, iterations=0, lr=9.999999747378752e-05. Root cause confirmed by direct reading of main.py:103-119, showing an unconditional fresh-optimizer construction and model.compile() call on every invocation, with no branch for 'resuming' vs 'fresh'.
risks.mitigation: Not a launch blocker: this is not a newly-introduced risk unique to the full-corpus run -- it is the exact mechanism the pilot's real, completed, successful 22-epoch run already used throughout. The pilot's own real result is direct empirical proof this regime (weights persist, optimizer state resets every invocation) produces working, improving models for this architecture and task. Required action: correct the learning_rate_policy label and any monitoring documentation implying continuous cross-shard decay or optimizer-momentum continuity, before final model acceptance/publication (not before launch).

risks.title: The original audit's licensing finding was incorrect -- real LICENSE files exist and were not searched for
risks.severity: was classified HIGH/UNANSWERED, corrected to LOW for the code component
risks.impact: The original audit stated no LICENSE file was located for loghi-htr or the checkpoint. This review found real MIT LICENSE files for loghi-htr, laypa, loghi-tooling, and the umbrella loghi meta-repo (all Copyright (c) 2022 rvankoert), permitting use, copy, modification, distribution, sublicensing, and sale without restriction. This resolves the code-license question for private/internal use. The pretrained model WEIGHTS have no separately, explicitly stated license (distributed as part of the same project, plausibly but not confirmed to follow the same terms). The training dataset's own license/permission terms remain genuinely unanswered -- no documentation of this was found anywhere in the repository.
risks.evidence: .loghi-upstream/LICENSE, .loghi-upstream/loghi-htr/LICENSE, .loghi-upstream/laypa/LICENSE, .loghi-upstream/loghi-tooling/LICENSE -- all read directly, all real MIT License text with a real copyright holder named. .loghi-upstream/pretrained-models/loghi-htr/generic-2023-02-15/file.txt also found and read: the real training configuration used to produce this checkpoint, including its own real training-data source list.
risks.mitigation: Code license: resolved, MIT, permissive. Weights license: recommend an explicit confirmation from the upstream KNAW-HuC Loghi project before any public release, publication, or commercial redistribution of derivative weights (not needed for private/internal use). Dataset license: recommend locating the actual data-use agreement/permission this project already operates under (outside this repository's own files) and citing it, since this audit could not locate it.
risks.status: resolved for code; open for weights (public use only) and dataset
risks.verification_method: Direct file search (find -iname 'LICENSE*') and direct reading of the found files, which the original audit did not perform.
